turns.response_html:
The rear assembly of the Iowa State University Formula SAE (FSAE) vehicle showcases a complex integration of mechanical engineering and custom fabrication designed for high-performance autocross competition.

Suspension Architecture

The configuration utilizes a double-wishbone (A-arm) suspension coupled with a pushrod-actuated inboard damping system.

  • Dampers: The gold-bodied units appear to be high-end Öhlins TTX25 or similar nitrogen-charged shocks. Placing these inboard reduces unsprung mass and allows for more aerodynamic flexibility.
  • Bellcranks/Rockers: The CNC-machined aluminum rockers translate the linear motion of the pushrods into the dampers. The geometry of these rockers is critical for establishing the motion ratio, which determines the effective wheel rate ($K_{eff}$) based on the physical spring rate ($K_s$): $$K_{eff} = K_s \times (MR)^2$$
  • Anti-Roll Bar: A splined anti-roll bar is visible, allowing the team to fine-tune the lateral roll stiffness and balance oversteer/understeer characteristics.

Drivetrain & Power Delivery

The "business end" of the vehicle focuses on maximizing traction and efficient power transfer.

  • Differential: Centrally mounted is what appears to be a Drexler Limited Slip Differential (LSD) or a similar custom-housed unit. This is essential for managing torque distribution across the Hoosier racing slicks during tight cornering.
  • Drive Axles: Constant Velocity (CV) joints are used to maintain power delivery through varying suspension travel and articulation.
  • Chain Guard: The red component labeled "BAD GIRL" serves as a protective guard for the drive chain and sprocket. This is a vital safety feature to contain the chain in the event of a failure at high RPM.

Materials and Fabrication

The assembly demonstrates a mix of fabrication techniques:

  • Chassis: TIG-welded 4130 chromoly steel tubing forms the spaceframe.
  • Unsprung Mass: The use of lightweight alloys for the uprights and rockers highlights a focus on minimizing inertia to improve tire contact patch consistency.
  • Tires: The vehicle is shod with Hoosier R25B (or similar) racing slicks, which provide the high lateral G-loading capabilities required for FSAE courses.

The attention to detail in the packaging—specifically the tight clearance between the exhaust, cooling lines, and suspension members—reflects the rigorous iterative design process characteristic of the Cyclone Racing team.
